title: Two Sum
problemStatement: Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to `target`. You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

examples.explanation: Because nums[0] (2) + nums[1] (7) == 9, we return indices [0, 1].

approaches.name: Brute Force Approach
algorithm: Iterate through the array using a nested loop structure.
The outer loop uses index `i` from 0 to N-2.
The inner loop uses index `j` from `i + 1` to N-1.
For every pair (nums[i], nums[j]), check if their sum equals the `target`.
If the sum matches, return the indices `[i, j]`.

approaches.name: Optimal Approach (One-Pass Hash Map)
algorithm: Initialize a hash map (dictionary) to store numbers encountered so far, mapping the number value to its index.
Iterate through the array `nums` once using index `i`.
For the current number `nums[i]`, calculate the required `complement` needed: `complement = target - nums[i]`.
Check if the `complement` already exists as a key in the hash map.
If the complement is found, we have located the pair. Return the index stored for the complement and the current index `i`.
If the complement is not found, add the current number and its index to the hash map: `map[nums[i]] = i`.
